thread:
Emily S: quick post — finished the dry run of the multi-region failover harness, sharing raw notes + commands. TL;DR: kernel-selection mismatch + KV-cache warmup differences caused a 15-20% tail latency regression in eu-west during drain.
Priya: link? where are the logs/artifacts?
Emily S: uploaded to gs://redwood-ci/perf/dryruns/1769004321/ — main files: run.meta, perf.jsonl, kernels.log, kv-stats.csv
Dan: nice. did you use synthetic qps or the replay harness?
Emily S: both. synthetic generator at 200rps/region for 30m, replay harness using last weeks traffic slice (2026-03-07) for ~45m. We ran three configs: baseline (current kernels + batching), opt-kern (new kernel selector), and batching-tweaks (aggressive batching + request size cap).
Miguel: what was the kernel-selection change?
Emily S: selector now prefers fp16 fused attention on long-ctx models when sequence_len >= 1024 and batch <= 8; previously it fell back to generic matmul path. That helped on host-level throughput but caused odd cache eviction patterns across shards during region drain.
Priya: eviction patterns? can you paste kv-stats?
Emily S: kv hit rate by minute for eu-west in baseline: 99.6% steady; in opt-kern during drain we saw drops to 86% for ~3m, coincident with increased L2 miss and CPU scheduling jitter. kv-stats.csv: "minute,hit_pct,misses" line sample: "12:03,86.2,1423"
SRE-Jen: did the region drain replay use the same concurrency distribution as production?
Emily S: good catch — replay used exact timestamps but we normalized client concurrency to 1.2x prod to stress drains. Synthetic run used Poisson arrivals, replay used original inter-arrival times.
Marc: sounds like apples vs oranges — how are we doing apples-to-apples?
Emily S: we tried to keep model versions and routing tables identical. The main difference was kernel selector code path: opt-kern compiled with new cu kernels and a slightly different memory layout that affects KV cache LRU ordering. That is the likely root cause.
Dan: any perf regression in p50/ p95 numbers?
Emily S: p50 stayed within 5ms, p95 for eu-west jumped from 210ms -> 255ms during drain with opt-kern. p99 showed spikes to ~480ms for ~20s windows.
Miguel: can you share the profiling snippet?
Emily S: pasted snippet:
```
# perf sample hot functions (opt-kern, drain window)
40% runtime -> attention_fused_fp16_kernel
18% runtime -> kv_cache_eviction
12% runtime -> host->gpu memcpy
6% runtime -> scheduler_backoff
```
Priya: kv_cache_eviction at 18% is alarming. Any mismatch in shard affinity on failover?
Emily S: yes — when requests were re-routed from us-east to eu-west, the routing map assigned some sessions to different shard group ids due to our temporary fallback policy; this caused cache churn because the KV keys were spread.
SRE-Jen: what fallback policy did you use?
Emily S: zone-fallback -> region-fallback -> model-variant fallback. For the test, we enabled region-fallback immediately (0s) to maximize cross-region traffic.
Marc: maybe too aggressive. Suggest we run a controlled sweep: region-fallback delay at [0,3,10]s and measure KV hit rate and tail latency.
Dan: agree. also need to compare with old kernel selector but with the same fallback settings to isolate kernel change.
Emily S: planned matrix: 3 fallback delays x 2 kernel selectors x 2 batching modes (default/aggressive) x 2 traffic types (synthetic/replay). ~36 runs. Each run 20m.
Miguel: for batching heuristics, what changed?
Emily S: batching-tweaks: increased batch size cap from 32->48 and enabled dynamic batching threshold of 30ms (instead of 15ms). This reduced tokens/sec cost but increased latency variance.
Priya: did you collect token cost + CPU/GPU utilization?
Emily S: yes — perf.jsonl contains per-run stats: tokens_per_sec, gpu_util_pct, inferred_cost_cents. Aggressive batching reduced cost ~12% but in opt-kern+drain it amplified tail spikes.
infra-bot: build/1769004319 completed for branch perf/opt-kern — artifacts uploaded.
Dan: infra-bot confirmed, thanks.
SRE-Jen: another thought: are we using the same quantization profile across runs? different quantization can change kernel selection heuristics.
Emily S: we pinned quantization profile q4_0 for all runs. only kernel selector and batching params changed.
Marc: any mitigations found?
Emily S: quick mitigation: bump region-fallback delay to 5s & force shard-affinity-preserve flag in router (keeps session->shard mapping for 30s). Re-ran a quick 10m check: p95 reduced back to 220ms, kv-hit recovered to 98.9%.
Priya: nice. is affinity-preserve safe for long drains? might increase load on original shard.
Emily S: it's time-bounded (30s) and only active during failover windows, but we need further sims for long drains.
Miguel: action items?
Emily S: 1) run the full matrix (36 runs) overnight with affinity-preserve toggled; 2) add an instrumentation point to kernels.log to tag kernel choice per request id; 3) generate an apples-to-oranges report that normalizes for concurrency and arrival patterns (Dan to own).
Dan: I'll own the normalization scripts. Will run a joiner to align P50/P95 windows by request arrival quantiles.
Marc: set up dashboard panels for kv-hit, p95, p99, kernel-selector-ratio, and cost per token. Include region labels.
SRE-Jen: can we gate opt-kern behind a canary rollout with routing affinity off by default?
Emily S: yes, canary recipe: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% with affinity-preserve off, then flip to on if kv-hits stay >99% for 30m.
Priya: thanks — please add run ids to perf.jsonl and link them in the ticket.
Emily S: done: run ids are prefixed "dryrun-1769004321-<matrixidx>". I'll open a follow-up ticket with links.
Miguel: cool. I'll help triage kernel tag logs tomorrow. :+1:
